Swift legal accountability ensures dangerous individuals are removed from public circulation.

State actors execute a standard institutional loop, using formal legal enforcement to restore public order after criminal disruptions.

Actual Article Body:
By MARTIN ROBINSON, CHIEF REPORTER

Published:  00:04 AEST, 2 October 2026   |  Updated:  00:12 AEST, 2 October 2026

A Tube passenger has today been charged with the murder of a 'kind and caring' husband-to-be who died three days after he was badly beaten on his way home from the Notting Hill Carnival.

Thomas Jewitt, who worked in affordable housing, suffered serious head injuries after an alleged assault on the Central Line platform at Liverpool Street station over the August bank holiday weekend.

The 32-year-old, who had attended the carnival's family day, was taken to hospital in a critical condition and died three days later.

He had been due to marry his fiancée next year, leaving her, his family and loved ones devastated.
